**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

The document already meets our preferred IP position across §§ 13–15:

- **Customer Data / Customer IP (14.1):** Customer owns Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP; Vendor gets only a limited processing right to provide, secure, support and improve the Services *for Customer* — no assignment to Vendor.
- **Deliverables (14.2):** Customer owns each Deliverable on creation, with an express Vendor assignment, matching personnel assignments, and further-assurance covenant.
- **Vendor IP + licence-back (14.3 / 13.2):** Vendor retains only Vendor Technology (defined at 1.9 as pre-existing material, expressly excluding Customer Data and Customer-owned IP), and embedded Vendor Technology carries the § 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify, create derivative works and permit contractors to support it — exceeding our fallback.
- **No joint ownership (14.4):** Joint IP only by separate signed instrument identifying exploitation rights; feedback is voluntary and Customer retains unrestricted use of its own feedback.

I also checked for the usual leakage points — no aggregated/de-identified data carve-out, no model-training right (15.1 prohibits it absent consent), and § 10 preserves accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences and Customer Data on termination.
